newsitem.title: ITALY: Employers see Italy GDP growth less than Europe.
newsitem.headline: Employers see Italy GDP growth less than Europe.

text.p: Italian employers continue to see Italian GDP growth of "around one percent" this year compared to growth of "over two percent" in the rest of Europe, Giorgio Fossa, chairman of the Confindustria body said.
"We are therefore not hooked up to the phase of international development," he told the annual employers' meeting.
He said that while Italy had managed to get near the Maastricht deficit/GDP three percent goal, "this does not yet give any guarantees of stability."
He forecast public sector revenues rising by almost seven percent this year, to around 1,000 trillion lire, with fiscal pressure increasing "by over one percentage point."
But he said it would be "illusory" to count on a reduction in public spending while just waiting for a cut in interest rates which "have fallen, but much less than inflation."

Italian financial markets are expecting the Bank of Italy to cut its 6.75 percent key discount rate in the near future after preliminary CPI data from Italian cities on Wednesday pointed to May annual inflation falling to 1.5/1.6 percent from 1.7 percent in April.
